title: Cloud-cloud collisions in the Antennae galaxies: Does high-speed collision suppress star formation?
question: How the star formation rate on a sub-kpc scale and the star formation efficiency of a colliding GMC depend on cloud-cloud collision velocity and GMC mass across the Antennae galaxies

data.arrays: 12 m array, ACA 7 m array and Total Power array
data.angular_resolution: synthesized beam 0''.72 x 0''.56 (76 pc x 60 pc at 22 Mpc), PA -87.3 deg

what.value: Continuum-subtracted H-alpha flux map of the Antennae from MUSE

evidence.quote: We used a continuum-subtracted H$\alpha$ flux map of the Antennae galaxies created by (cite: Weilbacher+18) to derive the SFR.
For the MIPS 24$\ensuremath{\mu}m$ data, we used a background subtracted image created by (cite: Maeda+24).
The Antennae galaxies are nearby (22Mpc; (cite: Schweizer+08))

what.value: H-alpha extinction correction with 24 um, coefficient 0.031 +/- 0.006

evidence.loc: 3.1 SFR derived from Halpha, FUV and 24um flux

what.value: H-alpha luminosity to SFR conversion factor

evidence.loc: 3.1 SFR derived from Halpha, FUV and 24um flux

evidence.quote: (cite: Leroy+08).

evidence.quote: We also corrected for the Galactic extinction using $A_{\mathrm{FUV}}=0.41$mag estimated by (cite: Leroy+19).

what.value: Convolution kernels to match angular resolution between images

evidence.loc: 3.1 SFR derived from Halpha, FUV and 24um flux
evidence.quote: we convolved MUSE H$\alpha$ and GALEX FUV images using the kernel derived by (cite: Aniano+11)

what.value: Dust model (U_min, gamma grid on P24-R71 plane) used for the model-based cirrus estimate

evidence.quote: We also estimated the IR cirrus contribution using the dust model by (cite: DraineLi07).

what.value: alpha_CO range reported for the Antennae, 1.1 to 6.54 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1

evidence.loc: 4.2 Derivation of physical properties of the GMCs
evidence.quote: The values of $\alpha_{\mathrm{CO}}$ in the Antennae galaxies are reported to range from $1.1$ to $6.54$$M_\odot$(Kkms$^{-1}$pc$^2$)$^{-1}$ (cite: Wilson+03; Zhu+03; He+24)

recipe.method: uvcontsub, concatenate 12 m and 7 m pointings, tclean mosaic with Briggs weighting, multiscale then single-scale CLEAN with automasking, feather with TP, primary-beam correct

recipe.goal: derive SFR surface density map from H-alpha + 24 um
recipe.method: H-alpha luminosity corrected with 0.031 L(24um), converted to Sigma_SFR with the Murphy+11 factor; all images matched to 24 um resolution (~6 arcsec = 600 pc); FUV+24um used as a cross-check
key_parameters: images convolved with Aniano+11 kernels to MIPS 24 um resolution and regridded

recipe.goal: remove IR cirrus from the 24 um flux
recipe.method: Empirical: subtract stellar continuum with a 5000 K blackbody scaled by 2MASS Ks, scale cirrus 24/5.8 um ratio (mode in outer-region apertures) by 5.8 um dust intensity; model-based Draine & Li check
key_parameters: cirrus 24/5.8 um ratio taken as the mode of the ratio in outer-region apertures
assumptions: stellar continuum longer than ~2 um approximated by a 5000 K blackbody
PAH abundance fixed at 4.6% in the model-based method

recipe.goal: identify GMCs in the CO cube
recipe.method: Rosolowsky & Leroy (2006) significant-emission mask, then PYCPROPS decomposition (local maxima, watershed with compactness parameter)
key_parameters: mask h = 5 sigma, l = 2 sigma, sigma = 0.14 K

recipe.goal: measure GMC mass, radius and line width
recipe.method: PYCPROPS extrapolated, beam- and channel-deconvolved moments; luminosity mass M_mol = alpha_CO times summed brightness
key_parameters: alpha_CO = 4.36 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1, single value for the whole region
assumptions: 2D Gaussian surface brightness, eta ~1.18 in R = eta sqrt(sigma_maj sigma_min)

recipe.goal: estimate collision velocity and typical mass per aperture
recipe.method: Hexagon apertures (300 pc side) centred every 300 pc; median GMC mass per aperture; v_col = sqrt(3 sum (v_los - mean)^2 / N) over GMCs in the aperture
key_parameters: apertures with a single GMC excluded; keep N_ap f_CCC > 0.1 per Myr (560 apertures)
assumptions: GMCs move randomly in 3-dimensional space within the aperture

recipe.goal: relate Sigma_SFR to v_col and GMC mass
recipe.method: Plot Sigma_SFR of each aperture against <M_mol> and v_col, overall and by region; also <M_mol> divided into five bins

recipe.goal: estimate star formation efficiency per collision
recipe.method: SFR = eps_CCC <M_mol> N_ap f_CCC with f_CCC = sigma_c v_col n_ap, sigma_c = pi (2<R>)^2; solve for eps_CCC
assumptions: eps_CCC is the product of the star-forming-collision fraction and the converted gas fraction; the two cannot be separated

recipe.goal: test robustness to delta, compactness and aperture size
recipe.method: Repeat the main plots with delta = 1.5 and 2.5, compactness = 0.1 and 0.00001, and aperture sides of 200 and 400 pc

score_reason: ALMA data are public and the cloud-finding and aperture recipe is mostly specified with numeric results, but calibration provenance, line-free channels, mask details and region definitions are missing, and the SFR maps depend on several other archives.
rediscovery_reason: The CO(1-0) archival data are public and the GMC identification and aperture/v_col recipe are specified with numbers (1759 GMCs, 876 apertures, v_col 10-150 km/s), so the ALMA-derived core results can be redone, though full SFR comparison needs several other archives.
